task_summary: The agent had to read the spreadsheet in /app/spreadsheets/1_22-47_input.xlsx and fill F2:H20 with the sorted rows from column B, using helper names from column J as the priority order, skipping blanks, headers, and duplicate B/C pairs.

explicit: Generate Python code that reads /app/spreadsheets/1_22-47_input.xlsx and writes the completed workbook to /app/output/1_22-47_output.xlsx.

Populate the sheet-level answer range F2:H20 by sorting column-B rows with helper column J, skipping empty cells, headers, and duplicate items defined by identical B/C pairs; if J is empty, fall back to A-Z sorting.
implicit: Use the helper names in the order they appear in column J as the priority sequence, not just as an unordered set of names.
Keep the workbook comparison scoped to the first sheet and the exact verifier range F2:H20.
missed_implicit: Use the helper names in the order they appear in column J as the priority sequence, not just as an unordered set of names.
instructions.evidence: step 3: "Wait: 'Names listed in column J, include all matching rows and keep their original order from the source and do not sort within the group.' So all entries matching J names come first, in their source order."; step 3 code: "listed = [e for e in entries if e[0] in j_set]" and "sorted_entries = listed + not_listed". The ground truth instead places HAMAN before HAMMED, which follows the order in J, not the source order of all J-matches.

closeness_to_success.explanation: The agent found the right unique rows and wrote a workbook, but in step 3 it collapsed all J-listed names into one source-ordered block instead of preserving the helper-list priority order. The verifier failed on a single cell difference at G4, and steps 4-5 stopped exploring by declaring completion without checking the output against the grader.

superficial_cause.summary: The saved workbook had the wrong order within the J-priority group: it put HAMMED at G4 where the answer expects HAMAN.
superficial_cause.evidence_quote: test_stdout.txt:994:  Test case 1: FAIL — Value diff at G4: gt='HAMAN', proc='HAMMED'

root_cause.summary: The agent misread the sort rule and implemented membership-based grouping with source-order preservation across all listed names, instead of grouping by the order of names listed in column J. It then repeated the completion path without verifying the workbook, so the incorrect ordering was never caught before submission.
root_cause.evidence_quote: step 3: "listed = [e for e in entries if e[0] in j_set]" and "Wait: ... all entries matching J names come first, in their source order."

failing_test_evidence.what_verifier_checks: tests/test.sh:12-51 recalculates /app/output/*.xlsx and /tests/answer_files/*.xlsx, then runs /tests/evaluate.py. tests/evaluate.py:174-189 loads the ground-truth workbook and the produced workbook, defaults to the first sheet when no sheet name is provided, and compares only the cells named by answer_position. tests/evaluate.py:205-223 compares /app/output/1_22-47_output.xlsx against the answer workbook and reports the first differing cell.
failing_test_evidence.exact_failure_quote: test_stdout.txt:994:  Test case 1: FAIL — Value diff at G4: gt='HAMAN', proc='HAMMED'

super_capable_counterfactual.claim: If the agent had ordered the J-matched rows by the sequence of names in column J instead of lumping all J-matches together by source order, the trial would have passed.
super_capable_counterfactual.X: Change the selection logic to build three ordered groups for HASSAN, HAMAN, and HAMMED in the order read from column J, then concatenate those groups before the non-listed rows.
super_capable_counterfactual.Y: It used `listed = [e for e in entries if e[0] in j_set]` and then appended all listed rows together before the non-listed rows.

issues: The wording 'first entries written in column J' is ambiguous until the verifier/answer workbook is inspected; the ground truth resolves it to the order of names in J.

notes_for_aggregation: This is a pure logic miss, not a file-path or formatting failure: the output workbook existed and only the J-priority ordering was wrong. The verifier reported a single mismatched cell, G4.
